clue.text: She took gold, keeping mum

indicators.note: keeping means the first word holds the next one inside it here

parts.note: to have taken gold is to have come first, so won
mum, a mother, is ma

explanation.surface: An athlete won a gold medal while saying nothing about it.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun she stands for a female adult person, so the two are interchangeable.

clue.text: Feel elated, given minor part on broadcast

indicators.note: on places the first piece above the second in this down clue

parts.note: a walk-on is a small non-speaking stage role
to broadcast a programme is to air it

explanation.surface: An actor is thrilled to land a small role on television.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being blissfully happy, as if floating above the ground.

clue.text: Wonderful, but tricky?

definitions.meaning: wonderful in the sense of enchanting, as if by a spell
tricky in the sense of involving conjuring tricks

explanation.definitionFit: Something wonderful seems enchanted; something tricky, in the conjuror's sense, involves sleight of hand.

clue.text: Breathers in anatomy class? Silly reason — no oxygen!

indicators.note: silly means the remaining letters are jumbled foolishly
no means the named element is taken away from the word reason

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A student in an anatomy class gives a foolish excuse about lacking oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes O from REASON, leaving RESAN, which 'Silly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin anatomical name for the nostrils, through which air is breathed.

clue.text: Lessen strength of ale — vital change made at last

indicators.note: change signals that the words ale and vital are rearranged
at last picks the final letter of the word made

explanation.surface: A brewer weakens the ale and finally alters its vital character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges ALE + VITAL; 'at last' adds E, the final letter of 'made'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease pain or trouble is to reduce how severe it is.

clue.text: Mark's retained hard modern spelling of his second name

definitions.text: modern spelling of his second name

indicators.note: retained means the name keeps the next letter held inside it

parts.note: Mark Antony, the Roman general, has Antony as his second name
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A man named Mark keeps a firm, up-to-date way of writing his middle name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark's' is Mark Antony, the Roman general; 'retained' puts H inside ANTONY, giving the form now usual as a first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman's name is today usually written with an inserted h, the common current form.

clue.text: Monk kept out of sinful, sexy dance

indicators.note: kept out of means the monk's letters stay outside, enclosing the next word

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk
sinful means bad

explanation.surface: A monk is barred from a wicked, sensual dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept out of' sounds like exclusion, but here the monk sits on the outside, wrapped around the sin.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brazilian partner dance famous for close hip movements.

clue.text: A case of make-up being on the way out?

definitions.text: A case of make-up being on the way out?

parts.words: A case of make-up being on the way out?
parts.note: a small holder for cosmetics, with a joke that self-regard itself might be going out of fashion

explanation.definitionFit: A small handbag for carrying cosmetics, so a container for make-up.

clue.text: Circus performer, mug possibly, caught by a lion?

indicators.note: caught by means the word for mug is held inside the others

parts.note: a lion is a big cat
to mug someone is one way to rob them

explanation.surface: A circus performer might be robbed, or caught, by a lion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' and the question mark flag examples: mugging is one kind of robbing, and a lion one kind of cat. 'caught by' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbler or trapeze artist is a typical big-top act.

clue.text: Fail to pay for duck

definitions.meaning: to fail to pay, as with tax, is to dodge it
to duck is to dodge or sidestep

explanation.surface: Someone skips paying for a duck dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean dodging: escaping a payment owed, or sidestepping a blow.

clue.text: A number of tables available for maths lesson

definitions.text: A number of tables available for maths lesson

parts.words: A number of tables available for maths lesson
parts.note: a number listed in printed mathematical tables of the kind once used in school lessons

explanation.definitionFit: An exponent giving the power a base is raised to, traditionally looked up in printed tables.

clue.text: Emperor appearing somewhat enervated?

indicators.note: somewhat signals only part of the word enervated is wanted

explanation.surface: A ruler looks rather drained of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman ruler of AD 96 to 98, the predecessor of Trajan.

clue.text: Furnishing list of special events?

parts.note: relating to special occasions or events
a list set out in rows and columns is a table

explanation.surface: A diary listing upcoming celebrations.
explanation.definitionFit: A small piece of furniture brought out for use as needed, so an item of furnishing.

clue.text: Exciting net-play — lots of it

indicators.note: exciting means the letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A thrilling tennis rally at the net gives spectators plenty to enjoy.
explanation.definitionFit: In abundance, used after a noun to describe a large amount of something.

clue.text: One employed at home, an American, taking year out? About time

indicators.note: About means the remaining letters are placed around the next piece
taking with out means the year is removed from the American
out with taking signals removal of the year

parts.note: a New Yorker is an American from New York City

explanation.surface: An American home worker takes a year off, then returns after a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking year out' drops Y from NEW YORKER, leaving NEWORKER; 'About' puts that around T.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone working from home on a computer linked to the office.

clue.text: Snack brought in, arranged by judge'

indicators.note: brought in means the snack is placed inside the next word

parts.note: arr. is the abbreviation for arranged, as in music credits
a bite is a snack

explanation.surface: A judge has a snack brought in and set out for them.
explanation.definitionFit: An umpire or referee who settles disputes, so one who adjudicates.

clue.text: Particular element that's thin on the ground

definitions.text: Particular element that's thin on the ground

parts.words: Particular element that's thin on the ground
parts.note: a chemical element from a scarce group, the name suggesting uncommon soil

explanation.definitionFit: One of the lanthanide metals, traditionally hard to find in nature.

clue.text: Almost witness soldiers retreating somewhere in Egypt

indicators.note: retreating means the combined letters go backwards
Almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to witness a signature is to attest it
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Nearly seeing troops withdraw at a location in Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts ATTEST to ATTES; add OR and 'retreating' reads ATTESOR backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in the Nile delta where the famous inscribed stone was found.

clue.text: Offer to raise afterthought about disastrous revue

indicators.note: about means the turned letters go round the jumbled ones
to raise in a down clue means reading upwards, so the letters are turned round

parts.note: PS, postscript, is an afterthought at a letter's end

indicators.note: disastrous signals the word revue is wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone proposes adding a postscript about a revue that flopped.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to raise' turns the postscript upwards; 'disastrous' scrambles the revue, and 'about' wraps the one round the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To present food or entertainment is to put it forward.

clue.text: Soldier tackling two fellows, or picked up for offence?

indicators.note: tackling means the soldier takes hold of what follows, enclosing it

parts.note: a soldier ant is a kind of ant
F is an abbreviation for fellow, so two give FF

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means the word or is turned upwards

explanation.surface: A soldier takes on two men, or is arrested, for an insult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' turns the little word upwards in a down clue; 'tackling' has the soldier ant grip both fellows and that word.
explanation.definitionFit: An insult or slight is an offence to someone's dignity.

clue.text: Stalks sailor in slightly flashy night-spot?

parts.note: to stalk someone is to dog them
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: Someone follows a sailor into a rather showy nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'night-spot' looks like a club but is a point of light in the night sky; 'slightly flashy' means twinkling.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirius, the brightest point of light in the sky, twinkles a little at night.

clue.text: Raised problem about second-class security for prisoner

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the next piece
problem signals the word raised is muddled into a new order

parts.note: B is a second-class grade

explanation.surface: Someone raised a problem about second-rate security for an inmate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' jumbles RAISED into DARIES, and 'about' puts it around B.
explanation.definitionFit: An old slang term for handcuffs, which keep a prisoner secure.

clue.text: Bully for your astrologer!

parts.note: bully plays on someone born under the sign of the Bull, and on the mock-congratulating exclamation bully for you

explanation.definitionFit: Someone born under Taurus, the Bull, as an astrologer would classify them.

clue.text: Antiques perhaps suggested by 11

parts.note: 11 across names a small table; its first word read as a time word suggests old pieces from a past era

explanation.definitionFit: Pieces made in the style of a past era, which antiques typically are.

clue.text: Points to an oddly shaped bread

indicators.note: oddly here means the odd-numbered letters of the words are picked

explanation.surface: Someone points to a strangely formed loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking every other letter of 'Points to an', from the first, gives P, I, T, T, A.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat Middle Eastern loaf that opens into a pocket.

clue.text: Champion's lost crown, just missing the gold

indicators.note: lost crown means the top letter is taken off

parts.note: a champion is a winner

explanation.surface: A champion loses their title, just failing to win gold.
explanation.walkthrough: In archery the gold is the centre of the target; this ring is just outside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In archery, the ring next to the centre, so a shot there narrowly misses the bullseye.

clue.text: Make fine adjustment — it's originally too fragile

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of the word too

parts.note: fragile means weak

explanation.surface: Someone fine-tunes an item that is a bit too delicate.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a small precise alteration to something.

clue.text: On E, perhaps, always briefly run outdoors?

parts.note: E is short for East, and the East is also called the Orient

indicators.note: briefly means the word is shortened, the poetic contraction dropping the v

parts.note: always means ever

explanation.surface: Someone on ecstasy constantly runs about in the open air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' is a link; 'On E' suggests drugs. 'briefly' drops V from EVER to give the poetic E'ER.
explanation.definitionFit: To take part in a sport of navigating across country with map and compass.

clue.text: Soldier dons suitable American kit

indicators.note: dons means the suitable word puts on the soldier, wrapping round it

parts.note: apt means suitable
a para is a paratrooper

explanation.surface: A soldier puts on appropriate US gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipment or gear needed for a task.

clue.text: Where to raise stock, being traditionally neat

definitions.text: Where to raise stock, being traditionally neat

parts.words: Where to raise stock, being traditionally neat
parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so this is a place that raises livestock

explanation.definitionFit: A large farm, especially in the Americas, where cattle are reared.
